name: proof-bento
title: Proof bento
description: One grid for all your proof: a large quote, a stat that counts up, a rating, a row of customer logos and a photo, in tiles of mixed size.
docs: Pass title, an optional eyebrow and description, and tiles: objects told apart by kind. quote { quote, name, role?, avatar? } sets the words large with the person under them (the tile adds the quotation marks). stat { value, label, detail?, prefix?, suffix?, decimals? } shows one figure; a number counts up once as it scrolls into view, text such as '24/7' is set as written. rating { score, count, source, max?, href? } draws stars to the fraction and is read as one sentence ('Rated 4.8 out of 5 on G2, 2,140 reviews'); with an href the whole tile is one link. logos { title?, logos } takes the same { name, mark?, href? } as LogoCloud; every mark keeps its own width, so a narrow tile wraps them in a row and a wide one sets them in columns, and a wordmark is never squeezed into a cell. image { src, alt, caption, credit?, focalPoint? } fills the tile with a photo and puts the caption on a solid chip, so it reads on any picture; alt is required. Every tile has an id and takes span (1 or 2 of the four columns) and rowSpan (1 or 2 rows, from a desktop up). Tiles are placed in the order you give and never reordered, so the DOM order is the reading order: pair the spans until each row of four is full. Below a desktop (1024px) there are two columns and row spans are ignored, and a single tile that would be left alone in its row takes the whole row, so there is never a hole (a one-column quote that gets a row to itself is set at the wider size there). A quote is set largest on two columns and two rows, smaller on two columns and smallest on one, so give a one-column quote one short sentence. Figures are sized to their tile from the longest figure of that width, so '99.98%' fits and a row of stats stays level; counting is skipped under reduced motion and the final value is in the page from the first render. locale sets digits and separators (a tag the browser cannot read, such as 'en_US', falls back to en-US); labels carries the fixed words.
